html:
An earthquake on 5 February 62 CE that badly damaged Pompeii, Herculaneum and other towns around the Bay of Naples. Modern estimates put it at about magnitude 5 to 6.

Temples, houses and public buildings cracked or fell. Seneca described the quake in his Natural Questions; he reports that a flock of hundreds of sheep died, perhaps from gas rising from the ground. In Pompeii, a marble relief in the house of the banker Caecilius Iucundus shows buildings in the forum tilting during the shaking.

Nobody linked it to Vesuvius, which Romans did not know was a volcano. Seventeen years later, much of Pompeii was still under repair: some temples had scaffolding and workmen's tools. Then in 79 CE the mountain erupted and buried the towns (see Vesuvius buries Pompeii). Scientists now see the earthquake as a possible early sign of that eruption.
sum: An earthquake on 5 February 62 CE that badly damaged Pompeii, Herculaneum and other towns around the Bay of Naples. Modern estimates put it at about magnitude 5 to 6.
